title: Predictive maintenance in manufacturing: The operational value of continual machine learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.18636v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Predictive maintenance in high-volume manufacturing often faces a domain-incremental learning problem: as new product configurations enter production, prediction models must learn from newly available data while preserving performance on earlier configurations that remain in operation. In this paper, we empirically study the operational value of continual machine learning methods for addressing this challenge in predictive maintenance, using real-world maintenance data from Bosch. The setting at Bosch covers 25 product configurations over five years, which creates a practical challenge for predictive maintenance models, as such models must be updated with data from newly introduced configurations without reducing performance on configurations learned earlier, a phenomenon known as "forgetting". tldr: 本文基于博世五年间25种产品配置的真实维护数据，首次实证评估了持续机器学习方法在制造业预测性维护中应对域增量学习问题（即避免对旧配置“遗忘”）的实际运营价值。
